_comment: Primitive-adoption ratchet baseline (design-system consistency C1/T3.4). These are the counts of bespoke chrome (raw <button>/<input>/<textarea>/<select> outside web/src/ui/). The test in primitiveAdoption.test.ts asserts the live counts may only be <= these — a NEW bespoke element turns CI red. As S2 migrations replace raw chrome with the shell primitives (Button/IconButton, the shared form family Field/TextInput/TextArea/Select, Modal), RATCHET THESE DOWN (edit this file to the new lower number in the same commit). The numbers may only shrink. rawInput was tightened 149 -> 147 on 2026-08-22: the two units of slack meant the “a NEW bespoke element turns CI red” guarantee above was FALSE for form elements, and it had already absorbed a real one (ProjectionRulesPanel went 5 -> 6 raw inputs with CI green). Keep every counter at the measured actual — slack is not a safety margin here, it is a hole.
_commentsWereBeingCounted: 🪤 AND THE HOLE THIS FILE WARNS ABOUT WAS ALREADY 13 UNITS WIDE, by a route the warning did not anticipate: `scanPrimitives` read raw file text, so COMMENTS counted as bespoke chrome. A design note that writes out `role="dialog"`, or quotes the `<button>` it is telling you not to write, scored against the very budget it was explaining — documenting a decision made the rail redder and documenting nothing made it greener. Comments are now blanked IN PLACE (length-preserving, so line reports stay accurate) and the counters are re-measured through the scanner's own walk: rawButton 249 -> 243, rawInput 147 -> 140, rawDialog 1 -> 0. SIX raw buttons and SEVEN raw inputs in the previous baseline were sentences. Every counter is again at the measured actual, and the ratchet is now strictly tighter than it has ever been.
_andItAnswersTheNoteBelow: The `_rawButton_249_note` below ends by saying the PROXY, not the count, is the thing worth changing later — because it counts <button> elements as a stand-in for bespoke chrome, and a chrome-free semantic button scores as a regression while being the correct fix. This change does not fix that proxy; it fixes a smaller and more embarrassing thing sitting underneath it, which is that the proxy was not even counting buttons. It was counting buttons plus sentences about buttons.
_theRatchetCanGoRedWithNoRedPR: 🪤 A THIRD HOLE, and this one needs no slack at all — it is MERGE ORDER. The ceiling is read from the BRANCH (loadBaseline reads the working tree), so a PR that adds a button while its branch still carries the OLD, higher ceiling is green on its own, and a PR that lowers the ceiling is green on its own, and MAIN IS RED THE MOMENT BOTH LAND. That happened on 2026-09-18: #2980 (LMMV-4) added the local-model Test chip against the 243 baseline it branched from, #3007 (SSM-6) ratcheted 243 -> 242, both merged 13/13, and main then measured 243 > 242. It stayed INVISIBLE for four more merges because a branch cut before #2980 does not contain the new button and therefore still measures 242 — only branches that rebase onto main inherit the red, so the rail accused #3015/#3016/#3017/#2939, none of which had touched a button. THE TELL: two unrelated PRs failing this test on the same count is never two PRs, it is main. Fixed by adopting the primitive on the chip, not by raising the ceiling: it carries real chrome (bg-surface-high, rounded-pill, hover shade), so it is not the chrome-free exception the notes below record — the count returns to the measured 242.
_rawInput_136_note: 140 -> 136 (improvement-dsc6-searchfield-primitive-20260919). DSC-6's residual: the schema-driven provider form (pages/settings/ProviderConfigForm.tsx) was the last holdout of the raw-input drawdown, carrying a local `inputCls` chrome string that FOUR bespoke controls consumed — an enum select, a numeric field, the show/hide-secret field and the plain text field. All four now ride the shared family (Select / TextInput / TextInput+trailingSlot / TextInput) and `inputCls` is deleted; it was an `export` with no importer outside its own file, so nothing else inherited the drift. Re-measured at the actual through the scanner's own walk, and BRACKETED rather than assumed: a 135 ceiling fails with 'expected 136 to be less than or equal to 135', so the live count is exactly 136. WHAT THE PRIMITIVES GREW to make this possible, each in lockstep with this adopter and never ahead of it: TextInput took `type="number"` + `min`/`max`, `minLength`, `pattern`, `trailingSlot` and an explicit `id`; Select took the `surface` axis (it was the family's only fixed-FILL field, so a panel-on-panel form could not match its select to its inputs) and `id`; TextArea took `id`. WHY NOT NumberField for the numeric branch: the stepper's `value: number` cannot express "unset" and reverts an empty entry to the last good value, so an OPTIONAL schema bound would become permanent once typed — the stepper keeps its dense right-aligned role and this stays the full-width nullable numeric text field. THE `id` PROP ALSO CLOSED AN A11Y HOLE the migration surfaced: this form publishes its own visible <label htmlFor>, but the primitives' ids were internal, so the JSON rows (already on TextArea before this change) had a caption that named them for sighted users alone.
_rawButton_241_note: 242 -> 241 (bugfix-uxpolish-20260919-frontend-cluster). The count went DOWN in a commit that ADDED an interactive chip, which is the shape the note below asks for. #477 needed a task's tag chips to become controls, and they were inert <span>s sitting beside a project pill that was a raw <button> with the same pill shape, size and hover shade — two implementations of one control, one of which lied about being clickable. Rather than add a third, both adopt a new shared primitive, ui/FilterChip, which is where this rail wants such chrome to live (scanPrimitives returns [] for ui/). So TaskCard's project pill stopped being a counted raw button and the tag chips never became one: 241, re-measured through the scanner's own walk. NOT ui/Button, for the reason the two notes below already record: its smallest size is h-7 px-m with a centred label, and these chips are h-6 metadata pills sitting in a row of h-5/h-6 siblings, so adopting it would mean overriding the stock look rather than taking it. The kanban card renders the SAME component in its handler-less <span> form, because TaskBoard records that a control across a `draggable` element gets between the pointer and the drag.
_rawButton_242_note: 243 -> 242 (feature-ssm6-preview-card). 🪤 THE CEILING WENT DOWN IN A COMMIT THAT ADDED A BUTTON, and that is not a contradiction — it is the hole the `_comment` above warns about, caught in the act. Measured on origin/main the live count was 241, i.e. the 243 ceiling carried TWO units of slack, so the file's own guarantee ('a NEW bespoke element turns CI red') was already false for buttons: this change's +1 landed green and unrecorded. Re-measured at the actual through the scanner's own walk, WITH this change in: 242. THE ADDED ELEMENT is the Session Map rail's mark (SSM-6): each tick became a real <button> because the card's contract is 'hover OR focus' and the rail had no focusable element at all, so there was nothing for 'focus does not auto-open' to be true of. WHY NOT ui/Button, the same reason StepStack recorded below: it fixes height (h-7..h-12), centres its label and sets a pill/squircle radius — a mark is a 4px tick absolutely positioned on a hairline, so adopting the primitive would mean overriding all of it. It is also the chrome-free case that note ends on: the tick carries one token'd background and no border, shadow or padding.
_rawButton_249_note: 248 -> 249 (ux-fix-onboarding-steps-keyboard). This ratchet is a CEILING that normally only shrinks, so the increase is recorded rather than quietly taken. The added element is `StepStack`'s step-row header, which became a real <button> because a completed row already carried onClick + cursor:pointer on a div with no tabIndex, role or key handler — a WCAG 2.1.1 keyboard failure on the product's first screen. WHY NOT ui/Button: it fixes height (h-7..h-12), centres its label, sets whitespace-nowrap and a pill/squircle radius. A step row is variable-height (a done row adds a summary line), full-width and left-aligned, so adopting the primitive would mean overriding most of it — the opposite of adopting the stock look. AND WHAT THIS EXPOSES ABOUT THE RATCHET: it counts <button> ELEMENTS as a proxy for 'bespoke chrome', but this button carries no chrome at all — no colour, radius, border or shadow, only layout — inheriting every visual from its <li>. A chrome-free semantic button scores as a regression under the proxy while being the correct fix. The proxy, not this count, is the thing worth changing later.
